title: Proxima signs MOU with Lower Saxony for HTS tape production
summary: Proxima Fusion has signed a memorandum of understanding with the State of Lower Saxony in Germany to “lay the foundations for large-scale industrial production of high-temperature superconducting tape” in the region, the company announced. According to the announcement, the first two phases of the project, which will run until the end of 2029, will require a €140 million (approximately $162.3 million) investment, which is expected to be split equally between public and private funding. Lower Saxony has committed €21 million (approximately $24.3 million).

title: Reactor licensing, decommissioning, operational oversight regulations addressed in latest NRC rulemaking
summary: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission unveiled its latest proposed rule Friday, one that would overhaul broad swaths of its regulations on nuclear reactor licensing, decommissioning, and operational oversight. It also would impact both existing nuclear plants and new reactor applicants. The proposal, “Regulatory Enhancements for Reactor Licensing, Decommissioning, and Operational Oversight,” takes a similar approach to other proposed and final rulemakings issued this year in response to Executive Order 14300, “Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission,” with a focus on making affected regulations more flexible and open to risk-informed approaches.

title: Limerick’s digital leap: Sustainability through modernization
summary: Constellation’s Limerick plant has generated nuclear power in the community of Pottstown, Pa., northwest of Philadelphia, since the first of two boiling water reactors came on line 40 years ago, in 1986. The plan is to keep Limerick running for at least another 40 years, but from a control room that would look wholly unfamiliar to its 1980s-era operators. Limerick is set to get a major safety-related digital instrumentation and control modernization for its two units, rated at 1,153 MWe and 1,162 MWe, respectively.
